My computer is slow: what to try before you replace it

A slow computer is frustrating, but it does not always mean you need a new one. Try these steps first.

Restart it. It sounds obvious, but many computers run for weeks without a restart. A fresh start often helps.

Check free space. If your storage is almost full, the computer slows down. Delete files you no longer need or move photos to an external drive.

Look at what starts with your computer. Too many programs launching at start-up slow it down. Turn off ones you do not use.

Update it. Install pending updates for your operating system and programs. Updates fix bugs and improve speed.

Scan for unwanted software. Pop-ups, odd toolbars and strange behaviour can mean unwanted software. Use a trusted security tool to check.

Check your browser. Dozens of open tabs and extra extensions slow things down. Close tabs and remove extensions you do not use.

Consider the age. If the computer is many years old and has little memory, even a cleanup may not help much. Sometimes more memory or a faster drive can extend its life.

When to replace. If repairs would cost close to the price of a new one, or it no longer gets updates, replacement is usually wiser.
